clusters.name: Experiment with transformations in the plane

standards.description: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment based on undefined notions of point, line, and distance.
standards.ccssText: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc. (G-CO.A.1)

standards.description: Represent transformations in the plane and describe them as functions; compare distance-preserving and non-distance-preserving transformations.
standards.ccssText: Represent transformations in the plane using, e.g., transparencies and geometry software; describe transformations as functions that take points in the plane as inputs and give other points as outputs. Compare transformations that preserve distance and angle to those that do not (e.g., translation versus horizontal stretch). (G-CO.A.2)

standards.description: Describe the rotations and reflections that carry a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon onto itself.
standards.ccssText: Given a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon, describe the rotations and reflections that carry it onto itself. (G-CO.A.3)

standards.description: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles, and perpendicular and parallel lines.
standards.ccssText: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular lines, parallel lines, and line segments. (G-CO.A.4)

standards.description: Draw transformed figures using graph paper or geometry software, and specify sequences of transformations that carry one figure onto another.
standards.ccssText: Given a geometric figure and a rotation, reflection, or translation, draw the transformed figure using, e.g., graph paper, tracing paper, or geometry software. Specify a sequence of transformations that will carry a given figure onto another. (G-CO.A.5)

clusters.name: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions

standards.description: Use rigid motions to transform figures and to decide if two figures are congruent using the definition of congruence.
standards.ccssText: Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and to predict the effect of a given rigid motion on a given figure; given two figures, use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to decide if they are congruent. (G-CO.B.6)

standards.description: Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are congruent if and only if corresponding sides and angles are congruent.
standards.ccssText: Use the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions to show that two triangles are congruent if and only if corresponding pairs of sides and corresponding pairs of angles are congruent. (G-CO.B.7)

standards.description: Explain how ASA, SAS, and SSS triangle congruence criteria follow from the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions.
standards.ccssText: Explain how the criteria for triangle congruence (ASA, SAS, and SSS) follow from the definition of congruence in terms of rigid motions. (G-CO.B.8)

standards.description: Prove theorems about lines and angles, including vertical angles, parallel lines with a transversal, and perpendicular bisectors.
standards.ccssText: Prove theorems about lines and angles. Theorems include: vertical angles are congruent; when a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are congruent; points on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment are exactly those equidistant from the segment's endpoints. (G-CO.C.9)

standards.description: Prove theorems about triangles, including the triangle angle sum, isosceles base angles, midsegment, and centroid properties.
standards.ccssText: Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: measures of interior angles of a triangle sum to 180 degrees; base angles of isosceles triangles are congruent; the segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half the length; the medians of a triangle meet at a point. (G-CO.C.10)

standards.description: Prove theorems about parallelograms, including properties of opposite sides and angles, bisecting diagonals, and rectangles.
standards.ccssText: Prove theorems about parallelograms. Theorems include: opposite sides are congruent, opposite angles are congruent, the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, and conversely, rectangles are parallelograms with congruent diagonals. (G-CO.C.11)

standards.description: Make formal geometric constructions using compass and straightedge, paper folding, or dynamic software.
standards.ccssText: Make formal geometric constructions with a variety of tools and methods (compass and straightedge, string, reflective devices, paper folding, dynamic geometric software, etc.). (G-CO.D.12)

standards.description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.
standards.ccssText: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle. (G-CO.D.13)

clusters.name: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations

standards.description: Verify experimentally the properties of dilations, including effects on lines through and not through the center, and the role of scale factor.
standards.ccssText: Verify experimentally the properties of dilations given by a center and a scale factor. (G-SRT.A.1)

subStandards.description: A dilation takes a line not passing through the center of the dilation to a parallel line, and leaves a line passing through the center unchanged.
The dilation of a line segment is longer or shorter in the ratio given by the scale factor.

standards.description: Use similarity transformations to decide if two figures are similar, and explain similarity for triangles in terms of equal angles and proportional sides.
standards.ccssText: Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms of similarity transformations to decide if they are similar; explain using similarity transformations the meaning of similarity for triangles as the equality of all corresponding pairs of angles and the proportionality of all corresponding pairs of sides. (G-SRT.A.2)

standards.description: Use properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion for two triangles to be similar.
standards.ccssText: Use the properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion for two triangles to be similar. (G-SRT.A.3)

standards.description: Prove triangle theorems using similarity, including the side-splitter theorem and the Pythagorean Theorem.
standards.ccssText: Prove theorems about triangles. Theorems include: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two proportionally, and conversely; the Pythagorean Theorem proved using triangle similarity. (G-SRT.B.4)

standards.description: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems and prove relationships in geometric figures.
standards.ccssText: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems and to prove relationships in geometric figures. (G-SRT.B.5)

clusters.name: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles

standards.description: Understand that side ratios in right triangles depend only on acute angle measures, leading to the definitions of sine, cosine, and tangent.
standards.ccssText: Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles in the triangle, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios for acute angles. (G-SRT.C.6)

standards.skillName: Sine and Cosine of Complementary Angles
standards.description: Explain and use the relationship between sine and cosine of complementary angles.
standards.ccssText: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles. (G-SRT.C.7)

standards.description: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.
standards.ccssText: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems. (G-SRT.C.8)

clusters.name: Understand and apply theorems about circles

standards.description: Prove that all circles are similar using similarity transformations.
standards.ccssText: Prove that all circles are similar. (G-C.A.1)

standards.description: Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, chords, central angles, and tangents of circles.
standards.ccssText: Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords. Include the relationship between central, inscribed, and circumscribed angles; inscribed angles on a diameter are right angles; the radius of a circle is perpendicular to the tangent where the radius intersects the circle. (G-C.A.2)

standards.description: Construct inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle, and prove properties of angles for a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle.
standards.ccssText: Construct the inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle, and prove properties of angles for a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle. (G-C.A.3)

clusters.name: Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles

standards.description: Derive that arc length is proportional to radius and define radian measure; derive the formula for sector area.
standards.ccssText: Derive using similarity the fact that the length of the arc intercepted by an angle is proportional to the radius, and define the radian measure of the angle as the constant of proportionality; derive the formula for the area of a sector. (G-C.B.5)

clusters.name: Translate between the geometric description and the equation for a conic section

standards.description: Derive the equation of a circle using the Pythagorean Theorem, and complete the square to find the center and radius from an equation.
standards.ccssText: Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean Theorem; complete the square to find the center and radius of a circle given by an equation. (G-GPE.A.1)

clusters.name: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically

standards.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.
standards.ccssText: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically. (G-GPE.B.4)

standards.skillName: Slope Criteria for Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
standards.description: Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve geometric problems.
standards.ccssText: Prove the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines and use them to solve geometric problems (e.g., find the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line that passes through a given point). (G-GPE.B.5)

standards.description: Find the point on a directed line segment that partitions it in a given ratio.
standards.ccssText: Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the segment in a given ratio. (G-GPE.B.6)

standards.description: Use coordinates and the distance formula to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles.
standards.ccssText: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles, e.g., using the distance formula. (G-GPE.B.7)

clusters.name: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems

standards.description: Give informal arguments for the formulas for circumference and area of a circle, and volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone.
standards.ccssText: Give an informal argument for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone. (G-GMD.A.1)

standards.description: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.
standards.ccssText: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems. (G-GMD.A.3)

clusters.name: Visualize relationships between two-dimensional and three-dimensional objects

standards.description: Identify two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotating two-dimensional figures.
standards.ccssText: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of three-dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects. (G-GMD.B.4)

clusters.name: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations

standards.description: Use geometric shapes, measures, and properties to model and describe real-world objects.
standards.ccssText: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects (e.g., modeling a tree trunk or a human torso as a cylinder). (G-MG.A.1)

standards.skillName: Density in Area and Volume Models
standards.description: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in real-world modeling situations.
standards.ccssText: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations (e.g., persons per square mile, BTUs per cubic foot). (G-MG.A.2)

standards.description: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems involving physical constraints, optimization, or ratio-based layouts.
standards.ccssText: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (e.g., designing an object or structure to satisfy physical constraints or minimize cost; working with typographic grid systems based on ratios). (G-MG.A.3)

domains.name: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability

clusters.name: Understand independence and conditional probability and use them to interpret data

standards.skillName: Events as Subsets of Sample Space
standards.description: Describe events as subsets of a sample space using unions, intersections, and complements.
standards.ccssText: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or," "and," "not"). (S-CP.A.1)

standards.description: Understand and identify independence of two events using the product of their probabilities.
standards.ccssText: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if they are independent. (S-CP.A.2)

standards.description: Understand conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B), and interpret independence in terms of conditional probability.
standards.ccssText: Understand the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B), and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A, and the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B. (S-CP.A.3)

standards.description: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.
standards.ccssText: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities. (S-CP.A.4)

standards.description: Recognize and explain conditional probability and independence in everyday language and real-world situations.
standards.ccssText: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations. (S-CP.A.5)

clusters.name: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model

standards.description: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret the result.
standards.ccssText: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model. (S-CP.B.6)

standards.description: Apply the Addition Rule P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B) and interpret the result in context.
standards.ccssText: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model. (S-CP.B.7)
